script.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.

terra.problem: The unpacked-boxes joke implies Judah married quickly after moving, but the text does not say how much time passed.
Judah being one of Jacob's sons is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The text says Onan knew the offspring would not belong to him; it does not say he was unhappy about it.
Tamar's father does not appear later in the passage; it says only that she went to live in his house.
Judah thinks Shelah may die, but the explanation adds that he does not feel Shelah is safe at all and describes sending Tamar away as a way of keeping Shelah at a distance.
Judah's concern is a thought the text reports, not a reason he gives aloud. It also does not say he holds Shelah close.
The text does not say Tamar's waiting is over; it says Shelah has grown and she has not been given to him.
The explanation repeats the same veil-versus-mask contrast without adding insight or sounding conversational.
The passage does not establish whether a shepherd's daughter appears in the scene; it does not give Shua's occupation.
The explanation mechanically repeats the list of items without much of Papa Dorin's voice.
The explanation repeats the list of items rather than developing a natural explanation in Papa Dorin's voice.
The text does not say Hirah's journey was a long walk.
The men say no shrine prostitute has been there; the text does not say nobody there has seen Tamar.
The explanation invents why Judah does not mention Tamar and claims to know she is not in his mind.
The text does not say what is or is not on Judah's mind about marrying Shelah.
Saying Judah's admission was hard for him to say adds an unmarked assessment of his feelings.
Saying the midwife's announcement did not hold treats it as a prediction of the completed birth. The text says the first baby's hand came out and then his brother was born first.
The text does not say nobody anticipated what happened.
